accepted.reason: Microsoft announced a concrete inference-layer control that preserves content trust and provenance, adding independent product evidence to the broader shift from prompt-only defenses toward deterministic architectural enforcement.

The project supplies a concrete two-stage edge architecture, localized public-sector implementation, and explicit training/runtime privacy boundaries. It is publishable as an Interesting signal because rollout and quantitative effectiveness evidence remain pending.

rejected.candidate: AWS agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments
rejected.reason: A useful implementation pattern for externally enforced budgets and credential isolation, but primarily a partner solution and Marketplace integration rather than evidence of a new broadly available platform shift.

rejected.candidate: Grok 4.7 long-horizon agent evaluation on Amazon Bedrock
rejected.reason: A three-task AWS technical walkthrough with provider claims and a narrow evaluation; insufficient independent evidence for a model or agent-capability signal.

rejected.candidate: Orca Security natural-language security queries on Amazon Bedrock
rejected.reason: Customer-reported efficiency results compare against the team's own initial baseline and do not establish a general enterprise-security or agent architecture shift.

rejected.candidate: Microsoft AI-era networking and power infrastructure posts
rejected.reason: Useful architecture and strategy commentary, but no new generally available capability or independently assessable result met the publication threshold.
Operationally important migration notice with a clear January 2027 shutdown date, but a planned model-lifecycle change rather than a new structural AI, infrastructure, or governance signal.
